recipe.description: A recipe on GourMerge is a full repository: it has a title, ingredients, steps, variants, a version history, and can be remixed.
recipe.helpHint: Recipes work like GitHub repositories. Everything you know about forking, branching, and committing applies here.

fork.description: Create your own independent copy of someone else's recipe to adapt freely.
fork.helpHint: Remixing creates a personal copy of a recipe. Your changes stay separate from the original unless you submit a GourMerge Request.

branch.description: A parallel version of your recipe — experiment without changing the main version.
branch.helpHint: Think of a variant as a 'vegan version' or 'gluten-free variant'. Changes on a variant don't affect other variants until you merge.

commit.description: A named snapshot of your recipe at a specific point in time.
commit.helpHint: Every saved version stores all ingredients and steps as a snapshot. You can always go back and see exactly what changed.

merge.description: Apply changes from one variant into another, combining the best of both.
merge.helpHint: When you merge, GourMerge combines the ingredient and step changes. If two people changed the same ingredient differently, you'll see a conflict to resolve.

gourmergeRequest.description: Propose your improvements to the original recipe author for review and merging.
gourmergeRequest.helpHint: A GourMerge Request lets you share your recipe improvements with the original author. They can review your changes, leave comments, and merge them into the original.

diff.description: A side-by-side view of exactly what changed between two versions of a recipe.
diff.helpHint: The changes view shows added ingredients in green, removed ones in red, and modified ones highlighted. For step text, individual word changes are highlighted.

history.description: A timeline of all saved versions of this recipe, oldest to newest.
history.helpHint: Every time you save a version, a new entry appears here. Click any version to see the full recipe at that point in time, or compare it to another version.

explore.subtitle: Discover public recipes from the community.

conceptIntro.title: Welcome to GourMerge
conceptIntro.subtitle: GourMerge is like GitHub for recipes. Here is a quick overview of what you can do:

recipe.desc: A recipe is a full repository with ingredients, step-by-step instructions, and a complete version history.

fork.desc: Make your own copy of someone else's recipe and adapt it freely — the original stays unchanged.

branch.desc: Try a variation of your recipe (e.g., vegan version) without touching the main version.

commit.desc: Save a snapshot of your recipe at any point. You can always go back to any earlier version.

merge.desc: Merge changes from one variant into another — GourMerge handles conflicts for you.

gourmergeRequest.desc: Propose your changes to the original recipe's author — they can review, comment, and accept.

explore.title: Discover Recipes
explore.desc: Browse public recipes from the community — filter by difficulty, tags, or sort by popularity.

privacy.dataSessionDesc: HttpOnly, 14-day lifetime, set only when you log in
privacy.dataPrefsDesc: language selection, colour scheme (light/dark) and whether the introduction has already been seen. These cookies store only your preferences — no identifier and no personal data — and are necessary to operate the site.
privacy.dataContactDesc: name, email address and message content
privacy.dataRecipesDesc: recipes, versions, comments and ratings you create. Recipes marked “public” are visible to everyone together with your username.
privacy.purposeBody: The data collected is used solely to operate the GourMerge platform and to communicate with users. The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract) and Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interests). For enquiries submitted through the contact form, the legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR.
privacy.thirdPartiesBody: As a rule, data is not passed on to third parties. Exception: we use Sentry for error monitoring. When an error occurs, technical data (e.g. stack traces) is transmitted; the Sentry project runs in the EU region and the data stays within the EU. Transmission of personal data such as IP or email addresses is disabled in the SDK. Fonts are served from our own server — there is no connection to Google Fonts or any other external CDN.
privacy.right7: Lodging a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77)
privacy.rightsHint: To exercise your rights, please contact us via the contact form or by email (see below).
privacy.title: My data
privacy.subtitle: Request a copy of your data or delete your account. We send a confirmation email first, so we know the request really came from you.
privacy.typeLabel: What would you like to do?
privacy.typeExportDesc: You receive everything stored about your account as a JSON file (Art. 15 GDPR).
privacy.typeDeletionDesc: Your account is irreversibly anonymised (Art. 17 GDPR). You choose in the next step whether your recipes go with it.
privacy.sentDesc: If the username and email belong to an account, we have sent a confirmation email. The link inside is valid for 2 hours.
privacy.invalidToken: This link is invalid or has expired. Please submit the request again.
privacy.exportReadyDesc: We have also sent the link to your email address. It is valid for 24 hours.
privacy.deletionScopeTitle: What should happen to your recipes?
privacy.deletionScopeDesc: Your account is anonymised either way: username, email, display name, bio and avatar are overwritten. Contributions inside other people’s recipes remain, anonymised, so their history is not destroyed.
privacy.deleteRecipesDesc: All your recipes including branches and versions are deleted. Other people’s forks remain as independent recipes.
privacy.keepRecipesDesc: Your recipes stay publicly visible, but without any link to you.
privacy.deletedDesc: Your account has been anonymised. Thanks for being here.
privacy.retentionAccount: Account data: until you delete your account.
privacy.retentionContact: Contact enquiries: 12 months after the last reply, then deleted automatically.
privacy.retentionTokens: Confirmation and reset links: 24 hours at most; expired ones are removed automatically.
privacy.retentionLogs: Server logs: 7 days, then rotated out.
privacy.selfServiceDesc: You can trigger an export or a deletion yourself at any time, without writing to us:
privacy.retentionInactive: Inactive accounts: if you do not sign in for three years, we delete your account automatically. We warn you three times by email beforehand — six months, four weeks and 24 hours before deletion. A single sign-in is enough to keep the account, and the period then starts over. Only your last login counts, not opening an email.
privacy.twofaBody: You may optionally protect your account with an authenticator app (TOTP). We then store an encrypted key used to generate codes, plus ten recovery codes as hashes. No phone number is collected and nothing is shared with third parties — the codes are generated entirely on your own device. You can switch the feature off again at any time in your settings, which deletes the associated data.
privacy.deletionHard: An erasure under Art. 17 GDPR deletes your account for real rather than merely disabling it. Contributions that are inseparable from other people’s recipe history — versions someone copied into their own fork, and your GourMerge Requests and comments in their discussions — are reassigned to an anonymous placeholder account. Your name, email address and profile are removed entirely.

twofa.disableDesc: We ask for your password rather than a code, so a lost or broken device cannot lock you out of this setting.
twofa.challengeDesc: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
twofa.challengeRecoveryHint: Lost your device? Enter a recovery code instead.
twofa.challengeExpired: Your sign-in attempt expired. Please sign in again.
twofa.usedRecoveryCode: You used a recovery code. Consider generating new codes in your settings.

passkey.title: Passkeys
passkey.subtitle: Sign in without a password — using your fingerprint, face or device PIN.
passkey.explain: A passkey stays on your device and cannot be intercepted or typed into a fake site. At sign-in it replaces both your password and your verification code.
